thread:
Maya: OK team — planning huddle. We need to pick final bets for next quarter for the Hosted surface. Main tension: SLAs (p99 latency + uptime) vs output quality (larger models / higher-compute configs) vs unit cost. Quick takes?
Alex: Agree. We also have engineering capacity constraints: two runtime projects (KV cache rewrite + continuous batching) land at same time. Can't do both big model and both infra changes in same sprint without more headcount.
Priya: From ML side: customers asking for better rerank quality and embeddings recall. For rerank, moving to a 7B fine-tuned variant yields ~6-8% lift on our evals but adds 1.8x token cost and ~2x tail latency on current infra.
Jordan: Operationally: SLA math is simple — if we push heavier models, our p95/p99 goes up. We can keep p50 low with batching, but p99 requires capacity headroom + isolation tiers. That means Dedicated or premium SKU.
Sam: Sales feedback: a few mid-market accounts asked for a "high-accuracy" Hosted SKU and are willing to pay 2-3x. They want predictable latency commitments (p99 under 300ms for short chats). This maps to a premium tier request, not standard free tier.
Lina: CS: enterprise POC for AcmeCorp tripped over rerank quality during pilot. They're OK with higher price if we can promise isolation/rollback and a canary path. They also asked for embedding vector size options to reduce cost.
Maya: Proposal: two parallel bets — (A) Launch a premium Hosted SKU (isolated capacity, model knob for high-accuracy rerank) with SLA + higher price. (B) Optimize default tier for unit cost: smaller quantized variants + smart caching for embeddings. We cannot do both fully. Thoughts on priority?
Alex: My vote is B first — optimize the default surface that affects most users and reduces unit cost. We can deliver caching + 4-bit quantized variants within quarter if we drop one infra rewrite (we should pick KV cache rewrite, not batching).
Priya: If we do B, we should still prototype the premium SKU as a lightweight canary: bundle a 7B fine-tune on a dedicated pool behind a feature flag. Canary metrics: relative accuracy uplift >=5% on customer prompt sets, cost delta <3x and p99 <500ms.
Jordan: Canary checklist (ops): 1) dedicated pool config 2) autoscale limits 3) circuit-breaker fallback to standard model 4) tracing + token-level cost logs 5) rollout window. We can do a limited canary in 2 weeks once infra pool is provisioned.
Maya: OK, concrete launch criteria for premium SKU: must meet two of three — accuracy uplift >=5% on our eval suite, p99 latency <400ms under canary load, rollback path validated by SRE. If only accuracy passes, we delay rollout.
Sam: That seems reasonable. Pricing suggestion: 2.5x on token price, plus optional reserved capacity for enterprise. I'll run it by top leads.
Lina: Also add embedding SKU options: default 512-d dims, low-cost 128-d option for similarity use-cases. We should include a migration guide for customers.
Priya: Implementation note: 128-d embeddings reduce index size ~4x — cheaper for customers and helps our mem limits. But we must expose eval metrics (recall@10) so customers can choose.
Alex: To hit B: timeline = week1-2 product design + infra config, weeks 3-6 implement quantization + embedding cache, week 7 rollout A/B to 10% traffic. Is that realistic?
Jordan: Tight but doable if we freeze scope: no new orchestration infra, reuse existing autoscaler, skip canary automation for first pass (manual rollouts).
Maya: Decision: prioritize B (default-cost optimization) as Q1 shipped slice, and spin a focused 4-week canary sprint for premium SKU prototype (feature-flagged) in parallel but limited scope. I'll create PRD and OKR subtask.
release-bot: deploy queued: hosted-default-embed-cache/feature-flag -> staging (sha: a1b2c3) :rocket:
Sam: I'll document the customer asks and pricing rationale for PMM. Also capture contract implications for SLA on premium SKU.
Lina: I'll prep migration notes and customer-facing comparators (cost vs recall) for next week's customer advisory.
Maya: Great — I'll post PRD draft by EOD and schedule a 30m sync with eng/ML/Sales tomorrow. If anyone has blocking constraints, flag here.
Alex: No blockers from eng if we freeze feature scope. I'll set a spike for quantized path Monday.
Priya: ML will prepare eval prompts and baseline numbers by Tuesday.
Jordan: Ops will reserve the dedicated pool capacity for the canary — ETA 48h after the spike.
Maya: Thanks all. Short action items: Maya->PRD, Alex->spike, Priya->evals, Jordan->pool, Sam/Lina->customer notes. Back in this thread for updates. :white_check_mark:
